content.prompt: Solve simultaneously:

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2^{3x}\div2^{2y}&=2^2\\2^{3x-2y}&=2^2\\3x-2y&=2\\11^{y-x}&=11^{-1}\\y-x&=-1\\y&=x-1\end{align*}$$
Substituting into the first linear equation:
$$\begin{align*}3x-2(x-1)&=2\\x+2&=2\\x&=0\\y&=0-1\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}13^{x+4y}&=13^0\\x+4y&=0\\(5^2)^{x+5y}&=5^1\\5^{2x+10y}&=5^1\\2x+10y&=1\end{align*}$$
Subtracting twice the first linear equation from the second:
$$\begin{align*}(2x+10y)-2(x+4y)&=1\\2y&=1\\y&=\frac12\\x&=-4\left(\frac12\right)\\x&=-2\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}2\times2^a-3\times3^b&=-11\\2\times2^a+2\times3^b&=34\end{align*}$$
Subtracting the first equation above from the second:
$$\begin{align*}5\times3^b&=45\\3^b&=9\\3^b&=3^2\\b&=2\end{align*}$$
Substituting into the original first equation:
$$\begin{align*}2^a+9&=17\\2^a&=8\\2^a&=2^3\\a&=3\end{align*}$$
